acs.text_first_line: AC1 Every active case carries a next action
AC2 The routing rules set it
AC3 Waiting is a valid next action
AC4 It is visible on the list
AC5 A rule with no timer takes the state's service level
AC6 No due date can be found
AC7 Working days skip weekends and bank holidays
AC8 A closed case has no next action
AC9 A repeated transition changes nothing
AC10 Two transitions at the same time
AC11 Cases open before the switch-on are filled
AC13 A role without Case record R
AC14 No RESTRUCTURE version in force

gap_rows.title: rwb-integration next action resolution: login, ownership of the read path, contract field names, operation names, Schedule values, message texts, legacy rule values and the timer vocabulary not settled
gap_rows.source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13 and 15; Ownership Map API row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action (owner P3) and tables rule_row and rule_package_version (P7), reference_row and reference_version (P3), job_catalog (P2) and feature_flag (PLT); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1, T3.2, T5.2, API-P2-009 and Appendix T-B; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.2, A2.7 and the requirements served; legacy RWB-E2-035 sections 3, 4, 7, 12, 13 and 14; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.5, §R7.2 and §R9
gap_rows.section: §3 Preconditions, §5 Exception paths, §11 Data, §12.1 to §12.7, §13 Solution plan, §14 Validation and messages
gap_rows.description: One combined row for the unsettled points of this key. (1) Login: no source names the per-service login of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the legacy story runs under the shared recovery service identity. (2) Ownership conflict: the Ownership Map keeps GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action with P3 (API Specification v4 x-module P3; Arch v5 slide 41, P3 owns the case, the CMMN state, the queues, the tasks, the allocation and the timers), while this work package assigns the story to rwb-integration; the ruling taken is that rwb-integration serves the path under /api/recovery/integration/v1 (DP-13) and rwb-case keeps the case row, the four next action columns and the write, and the map row must be corrected to record it. (3) Contract field names: the sources name the legacy Java shapes NextAction, RuleRow, RoleInfo and RuleRef and the LDM fields DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053 and DF-REF-002 to DF-REF-011, not the JSON field names of the P3 case read, the P3 case list, the P3 next action write, the catalog operation of RWB-P3-E2042-CON, the P3 reference data and parameter reads or the P7 decision log read; the write path of the fill is named by no source at all, and the rwb-access authorise contract that the resolve, the read and the fill call, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, is not in the contract-dependency row of this key, so it is named in section 12.2 and carried here. (4) Operation names: the legacy interfaces NextActionAssigner.assign and NextActionCheckStep become POST /next-actions:resolve, GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action and the fill POST /cases/{caseId}/next-action, and no source fixes the colon path or the choice of POST for the fill. (5) Schedule: the legacy step is JOB-05 Timer check, every 5 minutes on Quartz, and the target is a Temporal Schedule named next-action-check on rwb-integration; neither the name nor the catch-up window, the overlap window and the backfill limit is fixed by a source, while Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as retired durable timers with owner all and the Ownership Map ruling on the timer table retires JOB-05 and TimerDue. (6) Message texts: MSG-P2-023 is a new message of the legacy story and its text is the story master's, not the catalogue's, and the platform texts of MSG-GEN-004, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are reused here without a catalogue entry that names this key. (7) Rule values: package version RES-2026.12 and the rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 with their action, owner role and timer are legacy values of the story master; they are kept unchanged and must match the registry rows that RWB-E2-042 and RWB-P7-E2035-APP load, and the legacy Background of RWB-E2-035 gives R-SET-13 the version RES-2026.12 while TC-E2-035-11 gives it SET-2026.12. (8) Timer vocabulary: the legacy calls the sweep JOB-05 and its step NextActionCheckStep, the timer table ruling retires JOB-05, and the name next-action-check is this work package's; the three vocabularies coexist in the legacy text of the criteria and are read as one mechanism.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-035 §12 names GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action and the interfaces NextActionAssigner.assign, TimerSpecResolver.dueDate, RuleCatalog.row, DecisionLogQuery.latestStateChange and ReferenceData.role; the Ownership Map row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action reads owner P3 with no ruling text; the work package JSON for RWB-P2-E2035 places all three stories in rwb-integration; legacy §4 step 7 names JOB-05 every 5 minutes while Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as retired durable timers owned by all; legacy §7 names the package version RES-2026.12 and the rules R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07; TSD P2 Integration v3 names no next action table and no next action endpoint, so the operation and table shapes have no technical source.

gap_rows.owner_role: Solution architect; contract owners of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision; platform workflow kit owner
gap_rows.proposed: Keep the story in rwb-integration as planned; serve GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action from the integration base under DP-13 and let rwb-case keep the case row and the write; fix the consumed field names in the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision contract baselines; fix the three operation names, the next-action-check Schedule values and the five message texts in RWB-P2-E2035-CON; carry the legacy rule values unchanged into the registry; correct the Ownership Map row so that the P2 service owns the read and the P3 service owns the write; and record in the timer register that JOB-05 is retired and next-action-check replaces its next action step.

asm_rows.text: rwb-integration runs as its own ACE database login with grants on its own schema rwb_integration only (DP-02), replacing the shared recovery service identity of the legacy story; the login follows the rwb_integration schema name of Architecture v5 slide 41 and is carried by the chart as a secret reference.
asm_rows.why: No source document names the per-service login, while DP-02 requires one login per service and Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41 give rwb-integration its own schema and task queue.

asm_rows.text: rwb-integration serves GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action under its own base /api/recovery/integration/v1 (DP-13) and resolves the next action, while rwb-case keeps recovery_case, the four next_action columns, the optimistic lock, the NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task and the write in the same transaction as the move; the Ownership Map row that keeps the read with P3 is corrected to record this split.
